Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
736 PM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A more widespread frost tonight east of the Blue Ridge where the 
growing season remains active. Otherwise, little to no change in the 
current forecast package. 


&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Frost Advisories again tonight before a warming trend kicks off 
the new workweek. 


- 2) Dry conditions persist with increasing temperatures through
  the end of the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Frost Advisories again tonight before a warming 
trend kicks off the new workweek. 

High pressure will continue to drift south and west toward the 
central Appalachians tonight yielding less of a marine influence due 
to westerly low level flow. This will set us up for one more good 
radiational cooling night with a classic ridge-valley split. Given 
the westerly low level flow and sharp surface inversion expect 
warmer temperatures over the mountains/ridges compared to the valley 
floors and colder rural pockets along/west of I-95. For that reason, 
Frost Advisories have been issued for portions of northern/central 
Maryland and northern/central Virginia where the growing season is 
currently active. The growing season has since ended in locations 
west of where the Advisories have been issued (i.e along and west of 
the Blue Ridge). 

Some subtle changes to temperatures have been noted in the near term 
based upon current hi-res guidance. Ended up with a blend of MOS, 
NBM 10th percentile, ConShort, and the regional Canadian to 
highlight the colder temperatures for areas points east of the 
mountains given the lack of a marine influence and SKC conditions as 
the high drifts overhead. Expect lows in the low to mid 30s in the 
Frost Advisory area as well as in the colder valleys west of the 
Blue Ridge. Mountain ridgetop locations and areas near the bay will 
see lows in the low to mid 40s. 

Warming temperatures kick off the new workweek given downsloping low 
level westerly flow. Expect high temperatures to rise above normal 
Monday and Tuesday afternoon with highs in the upper 60s and low 70s 
(low to mid 60s mountains). Minimal cloud cover and light winds out 
of the west and northwest will persist allowing a warmer airmass to 
mix to the surface. Expect seasonable temperatures to continue into 
Wednesday with even warmer weather arriving Thursday into late week. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions persist with increasing
temperatures through the end of the week.

Upper-level ridging builds over the Mid-Atlantic through the end of 
the week, resulting in continued high pressure and dry, stable 
conditions across the region. After a slight cool down Wednesday
behind the backdoor front, temperatures should gradually warm 
some, with afternoon highs reaching the mid-70s by Friday with 
overnight lows in the 50s. As the front stalls and starts 
lifting back north, some extra clouds may form in the warm 
advection pattern Wednesday into early Thursday. Mostly sunny
skies will return Thursday into Friday.

A few models point to this upper-level ridging breaking down 
into zonal flow overhead by the start of the weekend, although 
surface high pressure could linger for a bit longer. Overall, 
there is still no significant precipitation in the forecast 
through the end of the week, although will continue to monitor a
potential cold front off to the west that could approach the 
region by the end of next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected through at least 06z/2am. 
Meanwhile, the NAM and other hi-res CAM guidance continues to 
suggests at least a brief period of sub-VFR cigs and vsbys (fog) 
late tonight into early Monday morning, especially in locations west 
of the Blue Ridge and locations directly along the water. Confidence 
in fog development is medium given the modifying airmass in the low 
levels compared to the colder surface temperatures below. Winds will 
remain light out of the southeast this evening before turning 
westerly overnight. West to northwest winds are expected Monday at 
less than 10 kts. 

P6SM SKC conditions are expected Monday and Tuesday as high pressure 
drifts around the region. A dry backdoor cold front will cross the 
area late Monday night into Tuesday with a dry warm front lifting 
into the region Tuesday night into Wednesday. Expect a few passing 
high clouds and a wind shift with each frontal passage. Overall 
winds will remain light out of the west and northwest Tuesday before 
switching to the south and southwest Wednesday into Thursday.


&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Monday night with high 
pressure meandering nearby. Light southeast winds this evening will 
become westerly overnight into Monday. West winds Monday will 
become north to northwesterly Tuesday behind a dry backdoor cold 
front. No rain is expected with wind speeds less than 10 kts. 

Marginal SCA conditions possible Tuesday-Tuesday evening in NW flow. 
Marginal SCA channeling in south to southwesterly flow is expected 
late Wednesday into Thursday as a warm front crosses the region. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Light onshore or southerly flow will persist through this 
evening, and could result in one last round of at or near minor 
flooding along vulnerable shoreline this evening. A Coastal 
Flood Advisory has been issued for Alexandria for this 
evening's high tide, but it appears other locations will fall 
short. Computer guidance shows a steady decline in water levels 
the next couple days, with no additional flooding expected at 
this time.
